aeroelastic_stability.note: A completed static solve does not establish freedom from aeroelastic divergence.

independent_review.review_scope: Read-only review of the eight existing 200 m/s SOL144 response runs; no solver or divergence analysis was started for this review.
findings: All eight runs contain a nonzero aerodynamic stiffness contribution and factorization of the unsymmetric effective stiffness KSALL. This supports that the aeroelastic response equations were solved at the requested operating point.

Successful decomposition, no Nastran fatal, and a zero structural-singularity count do not establish that the operating point lies below the first positive aeroelastic divergence pressure. A nonsingular linear response can also exist beyond a stability boundary.
The effective matrix is unsymmetric. Zero diagonals, generic pivot signs, or the presence of factors are not a standalone positive-stiffness or aeroelastic-stability certificate.

No DIVERG eigenanalysis was requested in these inputs, and no critical divergence pressure or stability margin has been computed. The F06 structural singularity message is not a divergence eigenvalue result.

Every current case fails the existing small-translation, small-rotation and assumed-yield coarse screens. These failures already limit interpretation of the linear response; they do not by themselves identify static divergence.
The known MKL diagnostic and launcher return code remain recorded. Completion and load balance must not be relabeled as stability validation.

stability_method_reference.method: A separate SOL144 DIVERG request, selected through Case Control and paired with CMETHOD/EIGC, computes divergence dynamic-pressure eigenvalues for specified Mach numbers. The lowest positive root is the critical static-divergence pressure.

limitations: All ratios use actual independent solver results; no 100x response scaling is performed.
Small-deflection or elastic-screen exceedance is a physical interpretation limit, not a solver-completion flag.
Stress above the assumed yield is linear elastic extrapolation, not plastic stress prediction.
Centroid fiber checks do not prove mesh convergence, local buckling resistance or structural safety.
Static solution completion does not establish stability against divergence.
